sourceMap.disposition: The managed partial consolidates the six target-specific genAsyncResumeInfo bodies and the shared async-resume table/field helpers. Runtime Configuration dispatch retains each target algorithm and the explicit unsupported path.

target_ssize_t has universal long storage. Runtime target-width conversion/addition helpers preserve primitive overflow policy; the dependent array, field, VN, and decomposed-address consumers retain their target arithmetic and constant identities. No observable deviation is accepted.

Managed simd_t uses universal simd64_t storage while SimdStorageSize preserves native logical capacities (64 bytes on xarch, 32 on ARM64, 16 otherwise). Active vector payloads and typed VN identity remain limited to the native type size; this is an internal representation change, not an observable deviation.

Managed instruction-set identities are a union; generated per-target maps preserve native ordinals for flag storage and EE callbacks. Target-specific HWI ISA ranges are stored independently and selected through Configuration.

The managed instruction enum is the union of target identities. Generated maps translate before native-order table indexing, range checks, and ordinal arithmetic; the native CORINFO_InstructionSet ABI remains a separate target-prefixed alias enum.

The target-neutral emitter request enum is separate from xarch opcode metadata. Emission states use uint values 0/1/2, keeping DONT_CARE distinct for ARM selection; xarch metadata remains a 64-bit bitmask with unchanged values. No observable deviation is accepted.

The managed uint enum unions xarch bit flags, ARM32/64 option identities, and backend descriptor options. LoongArch/RISC-V I, C, and RELOC identities have suffixed names because their native ordinals differ; shared RC/RL values remain unchanged. INS_OPTS_ALIGN retains value 52, while its use remains guarded by FEATURE_LOOP_ALIGN until that feature-gating batch. No observable deviation is accepted.

Managed genTreeOps and the base VNFunc prefix are unconditional unions of GTNODE rows. The only conflicting row, MUL_LONG, differs by node type on ARM64 and 32-bit targets; metadata selects that type through Configuration while target predicates preserve inactive-node behavior.

Hardware NamedIntrinsic and VNFunc entries use the same deduplicated union order. HWIntrinsicInfo retains target-native row order and translates union IDs through generated forward/reverse maps; foreign-target lookups terminate with PlatformNotSupportedException.

Managed category ordinals and architecture-specific flag bits are disjoint universal identities; target-native metadata row order is still selected through the generated maps. Configuration-driven predicates preserve xarch, ARM64, and Wasm behavior, while xarch-only costs reject other targets.

HWIntrinsicInfo columns and names are emitted as separate target-native RVA spans and selected lazily through Configuration; instruction values are stored as target-native ushort ordinals and converted to the active target's existing instruction enum only at lookup. Per-target selectors keep foreign tables unreachable for linker trimming.

Value-number evaluator target branches and `gtFoldExpr` HWI dispatch use Configuration checks over universal intrinsic identities. The folding operation map and xarch float-comparison remapping are available in the universal build, with target algorithms guarded at runtime. Other tree evaluator entrypoints and Lowering cases remain FEATURE_HW_INTRINSICS-gated while their dependencies are migrated.
The managed enum is a union of shared, xarch, and ARM64 SIMD types; explicit target-native ordinal/count conversions preserve upstream type identities in value-number encodings.

The managed compiler retains GetLayoutNum/GetLayoutByNum as internal per-compiler identity tokens for zero-object value numbering and diagnostics; native uses pointer identity. This is an implementation mapping, not an observable JIT/EE difference.

Loop alignment is selected at runtime and enabled only for xarch and ARM64. The xarch path retains 15-byte descriptor chunks and its zero-sized remainder; ARM64 retains four-byte padding descriptors. Descriptor logical sizes use the configured target, and unsupported targets fail with CORJIT_SKIPPED.

Leaf constant costs use runtime target dispatch. Shared ARM predicates and RISC-V count planning are reused by the corresponding emitter helpers; Wasm SLEB sizing is shared with emission. Relocation checks preserve x86 and relative32 behavior. No observable deviation is accepted.

GT_CAST costs dispatch at runtime across ARM32/ARM64, xarch, LoongArch/RISC-V, and Wasm. Existing xarch width-specific and opportunistic-instruction-set formulas and the six-point overflow adjustment are preserved; unsupported targets fail explicitly. No observable deviation is accepted.

Math.Abs, saturating, common math, upper-SIMD save/restore, and floating negation costs now use runtime target selection while retaining their previous formulas. The existing FEATURE_SIMD runtime guard remains on upper-SIMD cases; no observable deviation is accepted.

Local-store and scalar binary costs now use runtime target/feature selection. Target-width long adjustments, ARM and xarch floating formulas, binary intrinsic availability, Swift return handling, and Wasm operand-order behavior are retained. Unsupported operator cases still fail through the existing unreached path; no observable deviation is accepted.

ARM and xarch call-cost adjustments, HWI feature dispatch and xarch intrinsic costs, the x86 long-vector adjustment, Wasm indirect-store handling, and multi-operand reversal now use runtime configuration. Existing formulas and explicit unsupported-operator failure behavior remain unchanged; no observable deviation is accepted.

Store-indirect cloning, 32-bit GT_MUL_LONG cloning, and Swift/Wasm leaf cloning now use runtime configuration. CPU_LOAD_STORE_ARCH is derived from the target, and RMW status remains observable only on xarch while the universal node shape carries the storage needed by xarch.

Integer-width, xarch SIMD-width, ARM64 scalable-vector, Swift, and Wasm diagnostic paths now use runtime configuration. Target-specific dump formatting and node-name behavior are retained; no observable deviation is accepted.

Target-specific node flags, call-convention labels, intrinsic names, conditional-compare flags, and HWI dumps now use runtime configuration. The disabled `verbose && false` internal-register dump was removed; no target-visible output changes are accepted.

Register-mask targets, single-register targets, fixed-out-argument targets, and xarch now select their existing ABI-location output at runtime. Register enumeration and printed diagnostic strings remain unchanged.

Register and scalar-mask enum members use prefix-first target identities (`X64` and `ARM32` for AMD64 and ARM), with `SRBM_NONE` and `SRBM_STK` shared. Generated per-target ordinals, mask tables, factories, and aliases preserve native values. Legacy target-selected unqualified members remain temporarily for unmigrated consumers.

Register-name interpretation uses runtime target configuration because equal numeric values from different register enums carry no architecture tag. Generated fixed-register switches remain target-qualified and separate; Wasm keeps its type-bit/index formatting. The mask table remains target-specific and unchanged.

Generated target-qualified scalar-mask identities and per-target register-ordinal tables, then selected table/factory spans through runtime Configuration. A universal two-bank regMaskTP preserves 32-bit X86 truncation, upper-bank placement on targets with more than 64 registers, scalar bit-operation width, ARM32 typed-double rules, and Wasm's distinct storage semantics. LoongArch/RISC-V profiler-trash constants spell their FP argument masks directly to retain compile-time evaluation while matching the runtime argument tables. Fixed-register operations remain explicit on unsupported targets; no observable deviation is accepted.

Target names, mask formats, branch dimensions, register-validity checks, fixed return-buffer helpers, and Swift register masks select target behavior through Configuration. Existing fixed-return-buffer assertion continuations are preserved; unavailable branch dimensions terminate explicitly. Wasm register validity is decoded from the packed value-type tag.

Argument-register tables, membership predicates, and mapping helpers dispatch through Configuration using target-qualified register identities. ABI order and widths, ARM32 double-register pairing, fixed return-buffer indices, and x86 floating-argument assertion continuations are preserved; unsupported fixed-register paths terminate explicitly.

The floating return-register alias now selects the same target-qualified register through Configuration, retaining the existing not-available value on x86 and Wasm. Debug float names preserve ARM32 double-register spellings, ARM64/LoongArch register names, xarch SIMD prefixes, and lazy diagnostic-name initialization. No observable deviation is accepted.

Architecture metadata members with cross-target name collisions use architecture suffixes, while register and mask references retain the existing target-qualified generated identities and ordinals. Identical register navigation and argument-register-mask selectors use runtime Configuration dispatch. The shared Globals initializer requires exactly one target among X86, AMD64, ARM, ARM64, LoongArch64, RISCV64, and WASM32, and requires TARGET_64BIT to equal AMD64 || ARM64 || LOONGARCH64 || RISCV64; UNIX ABI flags are checked against their matching x86 target. LoongArch SIMD remains an explicit fatal unsupported path when selected; Wasm-only register helpers reject other targets. Unsuffixed consumers outside these directories remain deferred.

The native lower.cpp partial-constant helper is split across managed GenTreeVecCon mask extraction and shared Lowering.HardwareCreate logic, with distinct xarch and ARM64 entry points; virtual-call this-use ownership is in Lowering.CallTargets. lower.h has no separate managed declaration surface.
